patch.value: Reachable whenever a package releases twice in one calendar day, which the workflow supports by design through its max-suffix logic.
The version-derived release date refuses the same-day suffix the release workflow actually emits

The release workflow tags a second release on one day as v2026.8.24-2 and stamps that version into package.json. calendarDateFromVersion required a strict YYYY.M.D and threw on anything else, so the date-from-version flag failed hard on exactly the day a package released twice. That turns a stale heading date, which is what the flag exists to remove, into a broken release. Found by CodeRabbit on the fleet rollout of that flag, on pm-beads pull request 79, before any package could hit it. Verified directly against the published 2026.8.17 binary, where a suffixed release version exits 1 with the parser message rather than producing a heading. The suffix distinguishes releases, not days, so it is parsed and discarded and the date is the calendar day while the suffix survives in the version heading itself. Non-numeric suffixes such as a beta spelling are still refused, because those are prerelease identifiers rather than same-day counters and inventing a date for them would be a guess, and an impossible calendar date is still refused even when it carries a suffix.
A suffixed calendar version derives the calendar day and keeps its suffix in the heading, a non-numeric suffix is still refused, and an impossible date is still refused with or without a suffix
